title: A performance refactor of AdminPermission.projects split one combined Q filter into chained .filter(teams__members=user).filter(teams__access=ADMIN_ACCESS) calls, so read-only team members get admin rights on any project that also belongs to some admin team.

findings.explanation: The change only refactors ORM queryset filtering using Django's Q objects and chained .filter() calls with constant values (ADMIN_ACCESS, READ_ONLY_ACCESS). No raw SQL, no user-controlled input is interpolated into queries.

When both `admin=True` and `member=True` are passed, the new `else: pass` branch skips the team-access filter entirely, returning all projects the user is a team member of regardless of access level. The old code used a Q filter that still required at least one of the access conditions to match (ADMIN_ACCESS or READ_ONLY_ACCESS). The new code is functionally equivalent only if both flags being True is intended to mean 'no access-type restriction', but this is a subtle semantic change. If callers ever rely on this function with both flags set to enforce a specific access level, this could permit broader access than intended (CWE-863: incorrect authorization). The impact depends on how callers use this function.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify that callers always pass exactly one of admin=True or member=True. If both can be True simultaneously, confirm whether returning all team projects (regardless of access level) is the intended authorization policy. Consider adding an assertion or raising an error if neither admin nor member is True (both False case is unhandled). Document the expected call semantics clearly.
